signals.name: Micron
signals.label: Whale conviction fracturing even as Congress keeps buying
signals.detail: Soros added 7.9x (2,824 -> 22,422 sh, ~$25.9M) in Q2-2026, but Tepper cut his Micron stake 41% and Druckenmiller dumped it entirely the same quarter. Congress has been unusually active: 8 purchases vs 3 sales in the past 6 months (Reps. Newhouse, Rulli, Gottheimer, Sen. Whitehouse among buyers), some sitting on gains as high as +229% since Feb 2026 buys.
signals.takeaway: Chip-memory conviction is fracturing among whales (Soros in, Tepper/Druckenmiller out) even as Congress keeps buying — a name to watch for a re-convergence next quarter rather than a clean consensus signal today.

signals.name: Nvidia
signals.label: Sharpest whale divergence of the Q2-2026 cycle
signals.detail: Tepper added (+53,500 sh to 1,525,000, ~$305M); Dan Loeb (Third Point) exited 100% (sold all 190,000 sh); Soros bought NVDA puts (bearish overlay); Burry's SOXX short (~9% NVDA-weighted, via Substack, no longer 13F-reportable) is reportedly working after SOXX fell ~21% in July.
signals.takeaway: Three schools of smart money took three different sides on the same stock in the same quarter — treat as a volatility/conviction-dispersion flag rather than a directional signal. Nasdaq closed Fri 21 Aug at 26,180.46 (+0.43%), a modest rebound after the Aug 19-20 AI-valuation unwind that hit KOSPI and US tech.

signals.name: Warner Bros. Discovery
signals.label: Triple-whale convergence, post-merger-approval
signals.detail: Loeb (Third Point) opened a new $533.2M/20M-share stake; Einhorn (Greenlight) opened a new $59.9M/2.25M-share stake; Soros added to reach $39.7M/1,488,690 shares — all in Q2-2026, right after WBD shareholders approved the Paramount Skydance merger (23 Apr 2026).
signals.takeaway: An unusual cross-style alignment (activist/value/macro) on a single post-merger media name — worth its own watch card rather than folding into the AI-mega-cap noise.

signals.name: Alphabet
signals.label: Still the broadest whale magnet, but Ackman and Tiger Global both trimmed
signals.detail: Berkshire added 48,144,587 shares (+$21.1B, SEC EDGAR primary) and Loeb quadrupled his stake to 1,025,000 shares in Q2-2026 — but Pershing Square (Ackman) fully exited Alphabet the same quarter to help fund a Microsoft/Meta add, and Tiger Global trimmed its Alphabet position while rotating into AI-chip names (Cerebras, AMD).
signals.takeaway: Near-unanimous whale conviction now has genuine cracks (Ackman full exit, Tiger Global trim); still the most broadly held AI mega-cap, but no longer unanimous. Also the busiest single congressional name this run — Gottheimer and David Taylor both bought GOOGL in their August filings.

signals.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
signals.label: Congress + fresh whale buy
signals.detail: Congress: 39 purchases over the past year totaling >$1.297M, a consistently top-purchased name (Quiver). Whale: Soros opened a new TSM position in Q2-2026.
signals.takeaway: Durable multi-quarter congressional buying now reinforced by a fresh macro-fund entry — the cleanest picks-and-shovels AI-foundry overlap this run.

signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Rally extended into a third session Friday
signals.detail: SLV +4.47% Wed 19 Aug, +2.75% Thu 20 Aug, then +1.72% Fri 21 Aug to close at $62.72 — a third straight up session after the Treasury buyback surprise pulled real yields and the dollar down. GDX +9.42%/+2.59%/+2.98% and SILJ +9.55%/+0.67%/+0.95% across Wed-Thu-Fri; SLVP closed Fri at $40.85 (+1.44%). GC=F/SI=F futures are low-trust this run (thin/rolled contracts, revised bars) — GLD ($423.36, +1.95% Fri) and SLV are the cleaner proxies. 6th consecutive annual structural silver deficit underpins the move (Silver Institute/Metals Focus).
signals.takeaway: Three consecutive up sessions across SLV/GDX/SILJ/SLVP through Friday's close confirms this is not a one-day futures-roll artifact; VIX also fell back to 15.13 (-5.5%) Friday, consistent with the broader equity-risk-off episode fading rather than the silver move reversing.

signals.name: Energy Fuels
signals.label: Bridgewater's new stake rode out a Thursday risk-off dip and rebounded hard Friday
signals.detail: Bridgewater Associates took a new $2.3M/160,899-share position in Q2-2026 (SEC EDGAR), layering onto the CEO/director open-market buys ($12.70-13.08, 7-8 Jul) already on record. UUUU fell -6.40% Thu 20 Aug in the broad AI-fear-driven rare-earth risk-off, then rebounded +8.92% Fri 21 Aug to close at $15.14 (MP Materials similarly: -2.89% Thu, +9.10% Fri to $60.05) — both names round-tripped the sector-wide de-risking within two sessions.
signals.takeaway: A rare case of a macro whale and insiders both accumulating the same rare-earth name; the sharp Thursday drop and Friday recovery look like sector-wide beta rather than a fundamental reassessment of either UUUU or MP.

signals.name: Cerebras Systems
signals.label: Tiger Global's largest new Q2-2026 bet
signals.detail: Tiger Global Management opened a new ~$660M position in AI-chip maker Cerebras in Q2-2026 — its single largest new stake this quarter — alongside a new ~$392M AMD position, while adding 2.6M shares to Intel (now ~4.25M sh, ~$593M) and exiting AppLovin and trimming Alphabet.
signals.takeaway: Joins a broader whale-cohort rotation down the AI stack into chip/infrastructure names (Cerebras, AMD, Intel) at the expense of some mega-cap software/platform positions — consistent with the same rotation showing up across several other tracked funds this quarter.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway / Greg Abel

Discovery stake (+396,080 sh to 1,488,690, ~$39.7M), bought NVDA puts (bearish options overlay), and fully exited Fluor (FLR) — the opposite of Druckenmiller, who opened a new FLR position the same quarter.
